headline: Approved up to $1,500 from the Open Space Protection Fund to buy trail maps.
summary: Most of the discussion covered a proposed solar array at 49C Rear Rolling Ridge Road, including wetland buffer impacts and timber cut on Town land. Other items included a possible trail around Duck Pond, a new Planning Director, and a beaver dam flooding the Londonderry Country Club.
decisions: Approved up to $1,500 from the Open Space Protection Fund to purchase trail maps, 7-0.
Approved the minutes of the September 8, 2026 meeting as presented, with one abstention.
Appointed M. Speltz to vote for alternate member Elkel Bickford.
Agreed to invite new Planning Director Jacob LaFontaine to a future meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: M. Speltz moved to allocate an amount not to exceed $1,500 from the Open Space Protection Fund to purchase trail maps. D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
D. Lievens moved to accept the minutes of the September 8, 2026, meeting as presented. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The motion carried, with G. Harrington abstaining.
M. Badois appointed M. Speltz to vote for Elkel Bickford.
The Commission agreed to invite him to a meeting to introduce himself and discuss this.

plain_text:
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Draft Minutes
1 Present: Marge Badois, Chair; Gene Harrington, Vice Chair; Deb Lievens, member; Bob Maxwell, 
2 member; David Heafey, member; Michael Speltz, alternate member; Gary Della Grotta, alternate 
3 member
4
5 Absent: Elkel Bickford, member; Susan Malouin, alternate member
6
7
8 Call to Order and Roll Call
9 M. Badois called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m.
10
11 DRC – 49C Rear Rolling Ridge Road - Solar Array - Map 11 Lot 47
12 Ethan Beals of Hayner/Swanson Inc. appeared before the Commission representing Continental Paving 
13 Inc. to discuss a proposal to install a solar array on a parcel consisting of 3.7 acres in Litchfield and 48.7 
14 acres in Londonderry. The property is undeveloped and wooded, abutting the Continental Paving quarry 
15 to the north and northwest. 
16
17 They plan to install a solar array of 23 acres, with a total project footprint of 30 acres, 0.5 acre of which 
18 is located in Litchfield. The array will be on ground-mounted racking with small motors. The ground 
19 under the panels will be loamed and seeded. NHDES considers runoff from solar panels clean runoff that
20 will infiltrate back into the ground before leaving the project area. 
21
22 The project impacts wetland buffers in two locations: a 63,700-square foot impact in the central portion 
23 of the site and a 11,400-square foot impact in the southwestern portion of the site. There are no direct 
24 wetland impacts, and the panels and racking are out of the wetland and wetland buffer areas. The 
25 stormwater management area and a piece of the gravel road will impact the buffer.
26
27 E. Beals reviewed the proposed maintenance plan, as the vegetation would need to be low enough not 
28 to block the panels. They are consulting with Revision Energy about the type of vegetation to plant and 
29 the layout of the array.
30
31 The Commission asked that the site be mowed in late winter or early spring to avoid impacting ground-
32 nesting birds and small mammals. E. Beals said they are coordinating with NHF&G to do an ecological 
33 review of the project. There have been no endangered species hits on the property, only in the general 
34 vicinity. They opted not to fill the wetland, although doing so would decrease the footprint of the array.
35
36 The Commission noted the destruction of a wetlands finger by logging crews. E. Beals said trees can be 
37 cut in wetlands per New Hampshire law. Their wetlands scientist revisited the property two weeks 
38 earlier to confirm that the wetland was not impacted and the property has begun to revegetate. The 
39 root systems are still functioning; it would require several years for the roots to establish, if the area 
40 were replanted. 
41
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Draft Minutes
42 The Commission questioned clearing approximately 1/2 acre of Town-owned land near the Calpine 
43 transmission line. E. Beals said this was done inadvertently, as they believed it was part of the Calpine 
44 easement; however, this was incorrect. The wetland scientist said this area is also revegetating. The 
45 Commission stressed the need to determine the value of the timber taken and a means of compensating
46 the Town, and suggested conducting a site walk with the Town Forester.
47
48 Morgan Hollis of Gottesman & Hollis said they will compensate the Town for the error in the 
49 contractor's efforts regarding the timber trespass. He noted they did not know who would determine 
50 what that compensation would be. He reiterated that replanting was not needed in that location, per 
51 the wetland scientist; however, they would reforest the area, if required. He asked that the Commission 
52 coordinate the Town Forester visiting the area with E. Beals or Continental Paving.
53
54 The Commission noted that conservation plaques should be posted along the edge of the wetland 
55 buffer, not the edge of the wetland buffer impact. E. Beals said historically, they have been installed 
56 along the edge of the wetland buffer impact. The Commission clarified when the NHDES issues a 
57 wetland permit, the wetland boundary is changed; E. Beals will look into this.
58
59 The Commission asked about establishing the location of a gore on the Town line between Londonderry 
60 and Litchfield. E. Beals said bounding and providing formal boundary of a Town is a significant challenge; 
61 surveying one property does not locate the Town line on every abutting property. He said they will meet 
62 monumentation requirements for the subject lot; a Town line is not usually monumented as it bisects a 
63 property. 
64
65 Ryan Charbonneau of Continental Paving explained how the power generated by the array will be offput,
66 noting that entities have not been identified. 
67
68 E. Beals explained the gravel driveway crosses the wetlands at the narrowest portion via a historic 
69 culvert. He also explained the measures that will be taken to define the limits of the project in 
70 coordination with NHF&G. 
71
72 Commission Comments: Consult with Town Forester. Move the wetland buffer signs to the edge of the 
73 buffer. Ensure that the maintenance plan accounts for ground-nesting birds and small mammals. Share 
74 information about coordination with NHF&G with the Commission as it evolves. Extra care should be 
75 exerted to protect the existing wetland during the construction phase. Ensure that the project area is 
76 carefully delineated to avoid unnecessary impacts to the existing wetlands and buffers during 
77 construction. 
78
79 Public Comment
80 There were no members of the public present.
81

Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Draft Minutes
83 Old Business
84
85 Trail Work
86 M. Badois said Josh Cook with Trailways finished the work at the Mathes Trail. Al Sypek has been cutting 
87 blowdowns and trail blocks. 
88
89 Maps
90 M. Badois has ordered maps, but does not have an invoice.
91
92 M. Badois appointed M. Speltz to vote for Elkel Bickford.
93
94 M. Speltz moved to allocate an amount not to exceed $1,500 from the Open Space Protection Fund to 
95 purchase trail maps. D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
96
97 NHACC
98 M. Badois noted NHACC is November 7th.
99
100 Financial
101 D. Lievens reviewed financial statements up to August 2026.
102
103 DPW Requests
104 M. Badois asked DPW to help open the beaver dam, as it was flooding the Londonderry Country Club. 
105 She asked that the kiosk be moved to the top of the parking lot; however, the big sign was moved 
106 instead. She has also asked if the Scobie Pond Dock could be removed.
107
108 Trails Grants
109 M. Speltz reported the results of the trails grants that were supposed to be announced in August have 
110 not yet been announced. 
111
112 New Business
113
114 Pumpkin Smashing
115 M. Badois shared information on Hudson residents smashing pumpkins in a field to feed wildlife after 
116 Halloween. It is too late to coordinate this for Londonderry this year. She suggested doing it under the 
117 powerlines next year.
118
119 Duck Pond Trail
120 M. Badois reported Woodmont would like to put a trail around Duck Pond. She said it is doable, except 
121 for the south end. Woodmont would like Trailways and the Commission to be in charge of it; M. Badois 
122 noted the Commission does not have a workforce; they can offer direction, but not labor.
123
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Draft Minutes
124 New Planning Director
125 M. Badois met with the new Planning Director, Jacob LaFontaine, and noted the need to establish 
126 procedures so that the Commission is better informed on projects. The Commission agreed to invite him 
127 to a meeting to introduce himself and discuss this. 
128
129 Property Description
130 M. Speltz is working on a description for Ken Soroco's property, which will need to be reviewed by K. 
131 Soroco's attorney and the acting Town Manager. 
132
133 Approval of Minutes
134
135 D. Lievens moved to accept the minutes of the September 8, 2026, meeting as presented. B. Maxwell 
136 seconded the motion. The motion carried, with G. Harrington abstaining.
137
138 Adjournment
139
140 D. Heafey made a motion to adjourn. D. Lievens seconded the motion. The motion carried 
141 unanimously. 
142
143 The meeting was adjourned at 8:51 p.m.
